examples.ko: 그 사람은 말은 부드럽지만 속은 간교해요.
examples.en: He talks softly, but he is sly inside.
He is a person who made money by crafty means.

examples.ko: 영화 속 악당이 정말 간교하게 웃어요.
examples.en: The villain in the movie smiles so slyly.

examples.ko: 간교하게 굴지 말고 솔직하게 말해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't be sly, just tell me honestly.

examples.ko: 옛이야기에서 여우는 흔히 간교한 동물로 나와요.
examples.en: In old tales, the fox often appears as a cunning animal.

examples.ko: 그 상인은 간교해서 손님을 쉽게 속여요.
examples.en: That merchant is crafty, so he easily tricks customers.

explain: '교활하다'와 비슷하지만 '간교하다'는 남을 속이려는 나쁜 꾀를 말할 때 쓰고, 글이나 이야기에서 많이 보여요. 대화에서는 '교활하다'나 '꾀가 많다'로 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is close to '교활하다' (cunning), but '간교하다' describes a bad scheme meant to deceive others and is mostly seen in writing and stories. In conversation people may say '교활하다' or '꾀가 많다' instead.

examples.en: I missed the last train by a hair.

examples.ko: 그 선수가 간발의 차이로 일 등을 했어요.
examples.en: That athlete won first place by a narrow margin.
I just barely avoided the rain.

examples.ko: 시험 점수가 간발의 차로 기준에 모자랐어요.
examples.en: My test score fell short of the cutoff by a tiny margin.
I narrowly avoided hitting the car in front.

examples.ko: 두 팀은 간발의 차로 승패가 갈렸어요.
examples.en: The two teams were separated by a razor-thin margin.

explain: 거의 '간발의 차(이)'라는 모양으로만 써요. 아주 작은 차이로 결과가 갈릴 때 쓰고, '아슬아슬하게'와 비슷한 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is used almost only in the form '간발의 차(이)'. You use it when a very small difference decides the result, with a feel similar to '아슬아슬하게' (by a close call).

examples.ko: 어머니가 입원하셔서 제가 간병을 하고 있어요.
examples.en: My mother is in the hospital, so I am looking after her.
It is not easy to find a caregiver.

examples.ko: 간병 때문에 한 달 동안 휴가를 냈어요.
examples.en: I took a month off to take care of a patient.
I checked at the hospital how much caregiving costs.
I got really worn out taking care of my father.
The family decided to take turns caring for the patient.

explain: '간호'는 환자를 치료하며 돌보는 일까지 넓게 쓰고, '간병'은 환자 곁에서 먹고 씻는 것을 도우며 돌보는 일에 써요. '간병인', '간병비'처럼 함께 쓰는 말이 많아요.
explain_en: '간호' (nursing) can include medical care, while '간병' means staying by a patient and helping with things like eating and washing. It appears in set words such as '간병인' (caregiver) and '간병비' (care costs).

examples.en: The company's executives gathered for a meeting.
The new leadership was filled with young people.
The employees were surprised by the management's decision.

examples.ko: 사고 후에 간부진 모두가 직접 사과했어요.
examples.en: After the accident, all the executives apologized in person.
I heard they will change the management a lot this time.
The executives and staff had lunch together.

explain: '간부'는 한 사람에게도 쓰지만 '간부진'은 간부 여러 명을 한 무리로 묶어 말해요. 비슷한 말로 '경영진', '임원진'이 있고, 회사나 단체 이야기에서 써요.
explain_en: '간부' can mean one person, but '간부진' bundles several executives into one group. Similar words are '경영진' and '임원진', and it is used when talking about companies or organizations.

examples.ko: 신청 절차를 간소화해서 서류가 두 장으로 줄었어요.
examples.en: They simplified the application process, so the documents dropped to two pages.
City Hall simplified its complaint handling process.
I wish they would simplify the complicated rules.

examples.ko: 짐을 줄이려고 여행 준비를 간소화하려고 해요.
examples.en: I want to simplify my travel preparation to cut down on luggage.

examples.ko: 결혼식 절차를 간소화하는 부부가 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: More and more couples are simplifying their wedding procedures.
The company decided to simplify its approval steps.

explain: '간단하게 하다'와 같은 뜻이지만 절차, 서류, 제도처럼 단계가 있는 것에 잘 어울려요. '복잡하게 하다'와 반대이고, '절차가 간소화돼요'처럼 피동으로도 말해요.
explain_en: It means the same as '간단하게 하다' (make simple), but fits things with steps such as procedures, paperwork and systems. Its opposite is '복잡하게 하다', and you can also say it passively: '절차가 간소화돼요'.

examples.ko: 부모님은 제 일에 너무 간여하지 않으세요.
examples.en: My parents don't interfere too much in my affairs.
I don't want to get involved in other people's business.

examples.ko: 정부가 시장에 지나치게 간여하면 문제가 생겨요.
examples.en: If the government intervenes too much in the market, problems arise.
I heard the boss personally got involved in the personnel decisions.
I'm sorry for keeping on meddling.

examples.ko: 제가 간여할 일이 아니라서 가만히 있었어요.
examples.en: It wasn't my place to get involved, so I stayed quiet.

explain: '참견하다'는 필요 없이 끼어든다는 나쁜 느낌이 강하고, '간여하다'는 그보다 중립적으로 일에 끼어들 때 써요. '관여하다'도 같은 뜻으로 쓸 수 있어요. 보통 '~에 간여하다'로 말해요.
explain_en: '참견하다' (to butt in) has a strongly negative feel of interfering without need, while '간여하다' is more neutral about stepping into a matter. '관여하다' can also be used with the same meaning. It usually takes the pattern '~에 간여하다'.

examples.en: My arm feels itchy, maybe from a mosquito bite.

examples.ko: 목이 간질간질하면 감기가 올 것 같아요.
examples.en: When my throat tickles, it feels like a cold is coming.
My back is itchy but I can't reach it.
My head tickles as if a bug were crawling on it.
The tip of my nose tickled, and then I sneezed.
The child laughs and says the soles of their feet tickle.

explain: '가렵다'는 긁고 싶은 느낌이고, '간지럽다'는 살짝 건드려서 웃음이 나올 수 있는 느낌인데, '간질간질'은 후자 쪽의 가벼운 느낌을 나타내요. 목이나 코가 근질거릴 때도 써요. 말하고 싶은 마음을 비유할 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 비밀을 알고 있는데 말을 못 해서 입이 간질간질해요.
phrases.en: I know a secret but can't tell anyone, so I'm itching to say it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말하고 싶은 마음을 참기 힘들 때 써요. 입이 실제로 간지러운 게 아니라 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when it is hard to hold back the urge to say something. The mouth is not literally itchy; it is a figure of speech.

explain_en: '가렵다' is an itch you want to scratch, while '간지럽다' is a light tickling feeling that can make you laugh, and '간질간질' expresses that lighter feeling. It is also used when your throat or nose tickles. It can also be used figuratively for an urge to speak.

examples.en: The mosquito bite keeps itching.
My throat tickled, so I drank some water.
My nose tickled, and then I sneezed.
My back is itchy. Can you scratch it for me?
My hair touched the back of my neck and it tickled.
As the wound healed, it began to itch.

explain: '간지럽다'가 일반적인 말이고, '간질거리다'는 간질간질한 느낌이 계속될 때 써요. 사람이 일부러 간지럽게 하는 건 '간질이다'라고 해요.
explain_en: '간지럽다' is the general word, while '간질거리다' is used when the tickly feeling keeps going. When a person deliberately tickles someone, the word is '간질이다'.
